candidate.title: PSI-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina image explicitly groups PSI-seq and Ψ-seq. It depicts one route from poly(A)-selected, DNase-treated RNA through CMC/OH− treatment, fragmentation, adaptor ligation, reverse transcription and purification to cDNA. The left residue drawing is a legend; the three fragment/product examples are a mixed molecular population, not separately processed sample branches. The d_ records preserve that family-level drawing, including treatment before fragmentation. A disconnected psi_ interface records the primary-supported PSI-seq resolution: fragmentation precedes CMCT/alkali, followed by 3′ linker ligation, RT and truncated-cDNA isolation. These are two sourced representations, not a claimed physical sample split, extra pictured branch, or interchangeable workflow. No material is transferred between them. The distinct downstream PSI-seq local instances retain the fragment-first input history; their purpose correspondence to the drawing does not make the drawn local history applicable to PSI-seq. Ψ-seq remains a distinct explicit target. Targeted external research identified its primary publication (PMID 25219674; DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2014.08.028), but that publication has no source ID or content in the supplied frozen registry. Its inspected passages and the evidence-admission limitation are documented in research_psi_seq.json; they are not attributed to the registered abstract of PMID 26968262. The Ψ-seq scope therefore remains unresolved within this source-anchored artifact pending admission of the primary source. The RT panel is described relative to each RNA template: marked-template cDNA ends near an adduct, while unmarked-template cDNA reaches its template end; no absolute product-length ranking is inferred. The final depicted product is cDNA, not a fully specified sequencing-ready library. Downstream ribosome-profiling-derived library construction explains the PSI-seq endpoint-to-read interface only. ARTseq/Ribo-Seq is an embedded component, and Pseudo-seq/CeU-seq appear only as related methods outside this schematic scope.
